links.targetTitle: Pattern operates on borrowed USDS: minting draws vault debt

title: Grove's USDS is borrowed from Sky's Allocation Vault, so minting creates debt and burning repays it
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.1 describes minting as a draw, not a creation: `mintUSDS` operates by "drawing USDS from the **Sky Allocation Vault** into the buffer and transferring it to the Grove ALM Proxy," implemented as `proxy.doCall(address(vault), abi.encodeCall(vault.draw, (usdsAmount)))`.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.1.2 describes burning as repayment: `burnUSDS` returns USDS "from the Grove ALM Proxy to the buffer and burn[s] it to **repay Grove's USDS debt** in the Sky Allocation Vault," via `vault.wipe`.

This is the economic core of the Agent model. Grove does not own the stablecoins it deploys — it **borrows Sky's balance sheet** and puts the proceeds to work in the credit positions listed in its Allocation System Instances. Grove's return is the spread between what those positions yield and what the borrowing costs; Grove's risk capital is what stands between a loss on those positions and a shortfall to Sky.

Every other control in the Artifact reads differently once this is clear. The `LIMIT_USDS_MINT` rate limit is a **debt ceiling with a drawdown speed**, not a money-printing cap. The Encumbrance Ratio commitment (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.3.1) is a leverage covenant. The Freezer's mandate to halt on Risk Capital non-compliance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.4.4) is a lender's acceleration right. And Sky Governance holding `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the creditor retaining control of the facility.

The buffer as an intermediate hop matters too: USDS lands in the Allocator Buffer before reaching the ALM Proxy, so the vault's accounting and the operating balance are separate places.
description: mintUSDS draws from the Sky Allocation Vault into a buffer then transfers to Grove's ALM Proxy; burnUSDS returns it and calls vault.wipe to repay Grove's USDS debt.
